question: Review of Regulation (EC) No 816/2006

In the context of interinstitutional negotiations on Regulation (EU) 2025/26451 on compulsory licensing for crisis management, the Commission gave a commitment2 to review the operation of Regulation (EC) No 816/2006 on compulsory licensing of patents relating to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products for export to countries with public health problems3, in line with Article 19 of that regulation.

This commitment was given by the Commission as Parliament’s position regarding the need for amendments to the 2006 regulation was not reflected in the outcome of trilogue negotiations, despite the fact that the regulation has never been utilised since it came into force. 1.
Will the Commission provide a timeline for the review of the 2006 regulation?
Will the review include consultation with public health experts and civil society organisations to better understand the reasons why the 2006 regulation has not been utilised?
Following completion of the review, will the Commission propose amendments to the 2006 regulation in order to ensure that it can work to assist countries experiencing public health problems?

Regulation (EU) 2025/2645 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2025 on compulsory licensing for crisis management and amending Regulation (EC) No 816/2006 (OJ L, 2025/2645, 30.12.2025, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/2645/oj). 2 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0319_EN.html.

3 Regulation (EC) No 816/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 May 2006 on compulsory licensing of patents relating to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products for export to countries with public health problems (OJ L 157, 9.6.2006, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/816/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.7.2026) The Commission is committed to delivering a report to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee on Regulation (EC) No 816/20061.

The report is expected to focus: first, on determining the remuneration of the rights-holder; second, on the application of the simplified and accelerated procedure; third, on how well the requirements of the Regulation prevent trade diversion; and fourth, on how the Regulation has contributed to the implementation of paragraph 6 of the Doha Declaration on the Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights Agreement and Public Health.
The Commission will present this report in a timely manner and will consult relevant stakeholders in the process. At this stage, the Commission cannot pre-empt the findings of the report.
